operator_io_quirks: Tiny DB (item 8, review 7, useracct 7, trust 9 rows): original_values lists are short, so rng.choices(k=min(5,len)) often returns nearly all rows; no sampling cap matters.
Mixed quoting in DDL: item/review/useracct use backticks, trust uses double quotes; writer must replay sqlite_master text verbatim.
trust has NO primary key (pk=[]): sample_fresh_primary_keys must no-op on empty PK tuple, else all rows collapse to one.
trust has two FKs to the SAME parent useracct(u_id) (source_u_id, target_u_id): both draw from useracct.u_id final values; self-join semantics rely on overlap.
review.a_id is INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (rowid alias) but also has an explicit index idx_review_IDX_RATING_AID; harmless duplicate.
All declared types are INTEGER or varchar(N); no date/time/bool/bit/year columns, so Date/Time/Bool/Bit fuzzers never fire here.
varchar(20)/varchar(128) dispatch to String(length=20/128); title samples are short words, name samples are capitalized first names.
No NULLs anywhere (null_rate 0.0 on every column) despite nullable declarations; TS will still emit NULLs via String/Number dropout only if elements empty.
review.rating and review.rank are nullable INTEGER with small distinct sets (4 and 7); Number fuzzer will produce wide-range ints far outside [1,10].
FK graph is acyclic: useracct -> item -> review, useracct -> trust; table_order levels: [item,useracct] then [review,trust].
No views, no triggers, no CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE columns beyond PKs; drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op except on PKs.
All storage classes match declared types (integer/text); no affinity contradictions to survive.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on i_id/u_id/a_id (INTEGER, scale=0, precision unset): range [-1,1] full-range, list range [min(el), 1]; PKs get max_l0=inf so fresh draws dominate -> tiny ints like -1,0,1,2.
Number fuzzer on rating/rank/trust: same [-1,1] range, so values like 0,1,-1,2 appear; original 5..10 ratings never reproduced -> implausible values drive FN on rating predicates.
String fuzzer on title/name: 20% fresh random strings over a-zA-Z0-9() of length 0..20/0..128, 50% contaminate; names like 'Helen' rarely reproduced -> FN on name equality.
FK columns u_id/i_id/source_u_id/target_u_id draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement; since parents are tiny, child FK values are a small subset -> join cardinalities shrink.
review.a_id PK filtered by sample_fresh_primary_keys; with max_l0=inf and range [-1,1], duplicates likely -> many rows dropped, review may end up with <7 rows.
trust has no PK, so no PK dedup; but source_u_id/target_u_id drawn from useracct.u_id (7 values) -> many duplicate (source,target) pairs, no uniqueness enforced.
choose_table_sizes: 50% branch gives int(30*u + u2*200) ~ 0..230 per table; other branch level0=1+30u, level1 x4 capped 2500 -> review/trust can be much larger than parents.
Number perturbation (+-1,+-2 sequential draws) on PKs makes consecutive a_id values collide -> PK dedup drops rows, shrinking review below parent item size.
No Date/Time/Bool fuzzers fire, so no template/format misses; all misses are numeric-range and string-content implausibility.

Literal pool from train SQL will seed rating/rank/trust with real values (5,6,7,10) but Number list_max quirk (overwrite with full-range max=1) discards them -> pool values ignored for INTEGER columns.
String pool values (names, titles) survive as elements and are returned w.p. 1-p=0.8, so name/title equality predicates have decent hit rate; contamination adds noise.
Empty parent (if useracct filtered to 0 rows) yields NULLs in child FK columns despite NOT NULL -> insert failures skipped, further shrinking review/trust.
